record_type_quote: We conducted an independent close replication and extension Registered Report of Fox & Rottenstreich [1], as one of the classic articles of the partition dependence phenomenon.

targets.title: Partition priming in judgment under uncertainty
targets.evidence_quote: We conducted an independent close replication and extension Registered Report of Fox & Rottenstreich [1], as one of the classic articles of the partition dependence phenomenon.
targets.outcome_quote: Based on a pre-registered replication evaluation criterion, we concluded a mostly successful replication of the findings of Fox and Rottenstreich (2003). Specifically, we found support for partition dependence in scenarios from Study 1a Items 1 and 2, Study 1b and Study 3, with weaker effects, yet with no consistent support for Study 1a Item 3 and Study 4.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The overall verdict is mostly successful, expressly qualified as support for some studies and no consistent support for others; this is partial support rather than an unqualified successful overall replication.

reasoning: Identity and both authors verified in primary full-text XML. New American Prolific sample, completed Stage 2 report. Other cited partition-dependence studies are background rather than targets. Study labels follow those retained by the replication.
